stem:
Tejas starts factorising $90$ as $9 \times 10$ and wants a complete prime factorisation.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: $9 \times 10$ is already complete, because both factors are whole numbers.
Stop at $9 \times 10$, because $90$ is printed as the starting number.
Keep $9$ as it is and only split $10$, giving $90 = 9 \times 2 \times 5$.

teacher.key_rationale: Composite factors 9 and 10 must both be split until only primes remain: 2×3×3×5. Treating whole numbers as finished, stopping because 90 is printed, or leaving 9 composite all fail completeness.
